title: Queues and messaging in enterprise integration

videos.script: Under Rui's bus there is a queue manager. Every flow in lesson 8 moves its messages through IBM MQ, and Joana's new integrations will publish events of their own. {{mq}} A queue promises something simple. The message will get there, even if the other side is down. What it does not promise is that the message gets there once. {{crash}} A consumer that crashes after doing the work, but before saying so, is handed the same message again. If the work was recording a payment, the payment is recorded twice. {{duplicate}} This lesson is about making that safe. A consumer that remembers what it has already done. And an outbox, so that a database and a queue never disagree about what happened. You will see both in a short Python program, and watch a duplicate arrive and change nothing. {{outbox}} Then the messages that can never succeed. Rui found more than fourteen thousand of them, in a queue nobody watched. {{dead}} And last, order. Why two consumers can apply two price changes backwards, and why you almost never need order across everything. {{order}}
